stories.headline: Marvell shares stumble despite revenue growth
stories.summary: Oof. Marvell Technology beat revenue expectations in Q2, but its future outlook (we're talking fiscal 2028 here, quite a forecast!) didn't quite dazzle investors. The stock promptly tumbled 8% in premarket trading. It's a classic Wall Street move: "What have you done for me *lately*... and what are you going to do for me *way in the future*?"

stories.headline: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh to deliver key Jackson Hole speech
stories.summary: Grab your popcorn (or your portfolio): Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh is hitting the stage at the annual Jackson Hole symposium today. Historically, these speeches are where Fed chairs lay out their big-picture plans and policy intentions, so everyone will be dissecting every word for hints on interest rates and inflation strategy.

stories.headline: US Navy blockade slashes Iran's oil exports
stories.summary: Looks like the Trump administration has shifted tactics in the Iran conflict. After a bunch of airstrikes didn't quite work, the US Navy is now blockading the Strait of Hormuz, severely cutting Iran's oil exports. This is a big move in "economic warfare," hitting Tehran where it hurts: their wallet.

stories.headline: Hundreds of UK military veterans told they owe thousands
stories.summary: Talk about a gut punch. A clerical error means hundreds of former UK service personnel were overpaid on their pensions and are now being told they owe thousands back, with their current pensions cut. After serving their country, you'd hope for less administrative headaches.

stories.headline: Brits embrace beans and lentils to save cash
stories.summary: The cost of living crunch is real, and it's turning British dinner plates decidedly more, well, leguminous. Shoppers are buying more beans, lentils, and tofu, while cutting back on both real and fake meat. Good for the planet, good for the wallet – maybe not as exciting as steak, but hey, jumpin' beans!

stories.headline: Norway's King Harald V passes away at 89
stories.summary: A true royal story: King Harald V of Norway, who famously refused a string of European noblewomen to marry his school sweetheart, has died at 89. He experienced exile during WWII as a child and reigned since 1991, insisting his oath was for life. His son, Prince Haakon, is now the new king. Long live the new king!

stories.headline: US, South Korea, and Japan hold joint military drills
stories.summary: Three's company, especially when it comes to countering North Korea. The US, South Korea, and Japan are going ahead with trilateral military drills, just a day after North Korea threatened retaliation against "US hostilities." It's a clear show of unity and strength in a very tense region.

stories.headline: Bosnian Serb warlord Ratko Mladic dies at 84
stories.summary: The man behind some of the most horrific atrocities of the 1990s Bosnian War, Ratko Mladic, has died at 84. Convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre, he was a figure synonymous with the brutality of that conflict. His death closes a dark chapter for many, though the memories of his crimes endure.

stories.headline: Washington rethinks strategy to counter China in the Pacific
stories.summary: The US is realizing that just "showing up" isn't enough to credibly counter China's growing influence in the Pacific. This suggests a deeper strategic shift is underway to understand and engage with nations in the region more effectively, moving beyond mere presence to genuine partnership.

stories.headline: "Lightning raid" sees Bronze Age gold stolen from Spanish museum
stories.summary: In a move straight out of a heist movie, highly professional thieves pulled off a daring four-minute raid on Spain's Villena Museum, swiping one of the world's greatest Bronze Age gold collections. They were in and out before opening hours, leaving police baffled and historians heartbroken. Now *that's* a story!

stories.headline: Nepal floods claim over 500 lives, rescuers race against time
stories.summary: The Himalayan flash floods have unleashed devastating tragedy in Nepal, with the death toll now over 530 and nearly a thousand still missing. Rescue operations are continuing, but with warnings of overflowing lakes upstream, the risk of a second wave of flooding is terrifyingly real. A truly horrific disaster for the region.

stories.headline: Madras High Court judge questions Tamil Nadu FM's absence
stories.summary: In a bit of judicial sass, a Madras High Court judge dramatically asked if Tamil Nadu Finance Minister Marie Wilson thought he was "the King of England" to avoid a court appearance. The Minister is trying to quash an assault case, and the judge clearly isn't having any of it. Popcorn-worthy legal drama!

stories.headline: Pakistan Cricket Board considered pulling players over Imran Khan interview
stories.summary: Talk about off-field drama! The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) apparently thought about pulling its players from a Test against England after Sky aired an interview with Imran Khan’s sons, who voiced fears about their father's well-being. It highlights the deep political sensitivities that can even spill into sports.

stories.headline: Mangaluru railway bifurcation revives old state tensions
stories.summary: A proposal to split the Mangaluru region from the Palakkad Railway Division has stirred up old tensions between Kerala and Tamil Nadu. It's a flashback to nearly two decades ago when Tamil Nadu sought its own Salem Railway Division, showing how even infrastructure projects can become flashpoints for regional pride and politics.

stories.headline: Anthropic wins big, judge blocks Pentagon blacklist
stories.summary: Huge news for AI startup Anthropic! A judge ruled that the Trump administration illegally blacklisted them as a supply-chain risk, violating their constitutional rights. This is a major legal victory for Anthropic in its ongoing battle with the government and a reminder that even big tech companies can fight back.

stories.headline: GTA VI "Extended Look" is here, and it looks like a movie
stories.summary: Rockstar Games dropped an "extended look" at Grand Theft Auto VI, and everyone's saying it feels less like a game trailer and more like a prestige crime drama. They even debuted it on Netflix first! With a release set for late 2026 (after multiple delays), it seems they're building the most cinematic game yet.

stories.headline: Meta tries to fix its "pervert glasses" problem
stories.summary: Remember Meta's smart glasses that people worried could record secretly? Meta's trying to tackle that "pervert glasses" reputation head-on with a privacy fix: the recording light will now automatically turn off if you try to cover it. They're also launching a new marketing campaign. Good luck, Meta.

stories.headline: Bluesky adds an "algorithmic opt-out" feature
stories.summary: Tired of every post potentially going viral? Bluesky, the decentralised social media platform, is rolling out an "algorithmic opt-out" feature. It means you can post just for your followers, without your content being amplified by algorithms. A nice option for those who want to keep things a bit more chill.

stories.headline: Flatpak gets €500k boost from Sovereign Tech Agency
stories.summary: Good news for the open-source community: Flatpak, a system for distributing Linux applications, just got a €500k investment from the Sovereign Tech Agency. This is a significant injection of cash and validation for an important piece of infrastructure in the open-source world, helping to ensure its continued development.

stories.headline: Talent isn't born, it's grown
stories.summary: Forget the idea of innate genius: a new perspective suggests that what we call "talent" isn't a gift you're born with, but rather a signal that someone has been in the right environment. This idea emphasizes how much nurturing, practice, and the right surroundings shape elite performance, not just raw, inborn ability.

stories.headline: Dolly Parton becomes target of vaccine conspiracy theories
stories.summary: Even the beloved Dolly Parton isn't immune to the internet's darker corners. Influential right-wing conspiracy theorists are falsely claiming that the Covid vaccine killed her, despite her being a vocal vaccination advocate and philanthropist. It's a stark reminder of how misinformation spreads, even about universally loved figures.

stories.headline: Modern science has an incentive problem
stories.summary: Ever wonder why science sometimes feels stuck? There's a growing argument that the very incentives built into modern science—like the pressure to publish frequently or chase flashy results—might actually be hindering deeper, more fundamental research. It's about questioning whether the "game" of science is set up for true discovery or just keeping the academic wheels turning.

stories.headline: Nvidia reportedly buying Hugging Face for $13 billion
stories.summary: Hold onto your hats! There are reports that Nvidia, the chip giant, is acquiring Hugging Face, a crucial repository for open-source AI models, for a whopping $13 billion. If true, this is a massive move, cementing Nvidia's dominance not just in hardware but also in the essential infrastructure of the AI ecosystem.

stories.headline: Elon Musk's xAI accused of training Grok on child porn
stories.summary: Here's a horrifying headline: a lawsuit claims Elon Musk's xAI used both real and AI-generated child pornography to train its Grok models. This is a massive ethical and legal bombshell, highlighting the immense challenges and potential pitfalls in sourcing training data for large language models.

stories.headline: EU AI Act moves from idea to enforcement
stories.summary: Europe's landmark AI law, the EU AI Act, is officially getting real. It's moving from abstract legislation to concrete enforcement, meaning Brussels is about to figure out if it can successfully turn its sweeping rulebook into actual, actionable regulation for companies. This could set a global benchmark for AI standards.

stories.headline: Google's AI Mode wants to be your travel agent
stories.summary: Google is pushing its "AI Mode" beyond just information retrieval, positioning it as an AI travel agent. New updates mean it can now track flight prices, help you book hotels, and handle more of your trip-planning. Soon, your AI might be asking if you prefer an aisle or window seat for your next vacation.

stories.headline: Anthropic aims to let AI agents control the physical world
stories.summary: Anthropic is developing a new hardware standard designed to let AI agents interact with and control physical devices. This is a significant step towards a future where AI isn't just chatting with you, but actively managing smart homes, robots, and other connected tech. Welcome to the era of the truly 'smart' home, potentially.
